newsitem.title: UK: UK households more confident about economy - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK households more confident about economy - survey.

text.p: A rising number of households expect the British economy to improve over the next 12 months, the European Commission Confidence Survey for May shows.

The survey, conducted by GfK, found 39 percent of households expected the economy to get either a little or a lot better in the next year. In April, only 16 percent of households forecast any improvement.
Only 26 percent said the economy had picked up over the past 12 months but in April, the survey found just 21 percent of households saying things had improved.
In terms of personal finances, 24 percent of households said their financial position would improve somewhat in the next year, up from 17 percent in April.

Britain's households were also more optimistic about unemployment in the next year. About a third said jobless queues would shrink either slightly or sharply, while in April only 17 percent had forecast a drop in unemployment.
